CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  NOTICE N2M26-38

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE ALHAMBRA HOUSING AND COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE

  TUESDAY, April 7, 2026
  6:30 PM

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a regular meeting of the Alhambra Housing and
Community Development Citizen Advisory (HCDA) Committee will be held on
Tuesday, April 7, 2026, commencing at 6:30 pm, at Alhambra City Hall,
Conference Room A, 2nd Floor, 111 South First Street, Alhambra CA, pursuant to
the order of the Chairman of the HCDA Committee, the Alhambra City Charter, the
Alhambra Municipal Code, and Section 54596 of the Government Code of the State
of California.

ESTEBAN ALVAREZ, MANAGEMENT ANALYST
HCDA COMMITTEE SECRETARY

Dated: April 2, 2026
Notice No: N2M26-38
   AGENDA

HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  TUESDAY, April 7, 2026, 6:30 PM

  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA CITY HALL
  CONFERENCE ROOM A
  111 SOUTH FIRST STREET
  ALHAMBRA, CA 91801

 1. ROLL CALL:
  Lewis McCammon  Yvette Cardenas
  Andrea Giese  Renee-Marie Alvarez
  Manuel Armas

 2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES: Revised March 4, 2025; January 6, 2026; February
  3, 2026

 3. PROGRESS REPORTS - Attached for the Committee’s review are copies of
  the Progress Reports for those programs utilizing Community Development
  Block Grant and HOME Funds. All figures indicate the progress made and
  services rendered to date for FY 2025-2026.

  a. Parks and Recreation: Senior Case Management
  i. Case Management Clients Served: 86
  ii. Volunteer Hours of assistance donated: 70
  iii. Meals delivered: 3313
  iv. Telephone calls made: 773
  b. Community Development: Code Enforcement
  i. Total number of complaints investigated: 456
  ii. Number of complaints identified as Health and Safety: 43
  iii. Number of referrals to the Housing Dept programs: 3
  c. Community Development: Housing Rights Center
  i. Number of clients served (approximately): 262
  ii. A variety of issues were discussed including evictions, security
  deposits, rent increases, repairs, contract questions, etc.
  d. Community Development: Home Improvement Programs
  i. HOME Major Rehabilitation: 3 in progress, 3 completed, 0
  cancelled
  ii. CDBG Minor Rehabilitation: 3 in progress, 3 completed, 1
  cancelled

  Recommended Action: Receive and file informational reports.
 4. WORKING MEETING IN PREPARATION OF THE 2026–2027 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN

  The City is required by the Department of Housing and Urban Development
  (HUD) to prepare an Annual Action Plan. The City’s Annual Action Plan identifies
  programs funded with HUD resources, including Community Development Block
  Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships (HOME) funds, and outlines
  the community’s priority needs and proposed activities for the 2026–2027
  program year.

  This working meeting of the HCDA will focus on eligible activities under the
  CDBG and HOME programs and may include consideration of new or revised
  funding recommendations for both. Consultant Veronica Tam and Associates
  will attend and provide a presentation to the Committee on the 2026–2027
  Annual Action Plan. Community organizations and stakeholders have been
  invited to participate and provide input on community development priorities,
  housing needs, and fair housing issues within the City.

  Comments received from the Committee and the public will be considered as the
  City prepares the draft 2026–2027 Annual Action Plan.

  Recommended Action: Receive public comments and direct staff to incorporate
  all input received into the draft 2026–2027 Annual Action Plan for further
  consideration.

5. STAFF UPDATES

  Discussion from the Staff Members of any item(s) not specified on the
  agenda. Items discussed must pertain the business of the HCDA Citizen
  Advisory Committee.

6. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE

  Discussion from the public of any items not specified on the agenda.
  Comments must pertain to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory
  Committee. Public comments pertaining to the HCDA Citizen Advisory
  Committee’s business are welcome. Kindly limit all oral communications to
  five (5) minutes. Please complete a speak card prior to the meeting and
  submit the card to the Committee’s Secretary.

7. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE

  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the
  agenda. Items discussed must pertain the business of the HCDA Citizen
  Advisory Committee.

8. ADJOURNMENT
 Copies of the staff report or other written documentation relating to each item of
business described herein are on file in the Office of Management Services,
Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, CA, and are available for
public inspection during regular office hours from 7:00 am to 5:30: PM, Monday
through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior
the meeting, the person may contact Esteban Alvarez in the Management Services
Department in person at City Hall or at 626.570.5012 during regular business hours.
   OFFICIAL
  Revised Minutes of the City of Alhambra’s
  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Regular Meeting of March 4, 2025
  CITY HALL • 111 S. FIRST ST.

  Committee Chair Vallejos called the meeting to order at 6:33 pm.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Committee Members Present:
  Lewis McCammon, Vice Chair  Bonita Sharma-Ngan
  Yvette Cardenas  Renee-Marie Alvarez
  Michael Soto  Marc Tousignant

  Committee Members Absent: Bill Vallejos, Chair
  Andrea Giese

  City Staff Present:
  Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager
  Esteban Alvarez, Management Analyst
  Holly Chenh, Housing Assistant
  Fernando Perez-Garcia, Code Enforcement Supervisor
  Janine Pinto Senior Services Supervisor

2. Approval of Minutes: 9/5/2023; 5/7/2024; 9/3/2024; 12/3/2024; 2/4/2025

  Staff Liaison Alvarez informed the Committee that no meetings were held on 9/3/2024 and
  2/4/2025 due to a lack of quorum. However, since these meetings were noticed and posted
  online for the public, staff wanted to officially state for the record that the meetings did not
  occur, despite being posted and noticed to the community.

  Motion: Motion to approve minutes by Committee member Soto, and seconded by
  Tousignant. All present committee members approved; motion passed.

3. PROGRESS REPORTS

  Management Analyst Esteban Alvarez presented the Committee with most up to date
  progress reports for FY 2024-2025 for the Senior Case Management, Code Enforcement,
  Housing Rights Center, and Home Improvement Programs. Staff requested that the reports be
  received and filed by the committee.

  Committee Action:

  Vice Chair McCammon presented supplemental documents to the Committee regarding the
  Housing Rights Center and expressed concerns about the agency’s staffing levels and phone
  response times. Committee member Cardenas suggested exploring other agencies and
  resources to complement the Housing Rights Center’s services. Consultant Tam noted that
  additional resources for the community, as per her previous recommendations, are available
  and listed on the City of Alhambra's website.

  Page 1 of 3
  Motion: The Committee received and filed the informational reports.

4. WORKING MEETING IN PREPERATION OF THE 2025-2029 CONSOLIDATED
  PLAN AND 2025-26 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN.

  Consultant Veronica Tam presented to the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee on the
  Consolidated Plan and Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing, covering the CDBG and
  HOME programs. The presentation included an overview of the goals of these programs, a
  map showing low and moderate-income areas, potential uses for the funds, beneficiaries,
  current goals and priorities, program limitations, eligible public services and expenditure
  caps, as well as eligible activities and improvements. Consultant Tam also referenced the
  updated Low/Moderate Income Map and outlined the upcoming timeline, which includes
  presenting a draft to the Committee in April and a 30-day Public Review Period to follow.

  Committee member Renee-Marie inquired if CDBG funds could be used for a Dog Park.
  Staff responded that a Dog Park is already in development, with an expected opening date in
  Summer 2025.

  Vice-Chair McCammon asked if CDBG funds could be used for street lights. Consultant
  Tam stated that yes, CDBG can be used to improve street lights. Vice Chair McCammon
  also inquired with Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez-Garcia about whether the Fire
  Department conducts rental inspections. Supervisor Perez-Garcia responded that he was
  unaware of any such inspections being conducted by the Fire Department. However, he did
  mention that his department collaborates closely with the Housing Rights Center, receiving
  referrals from them and providing referrals in return.

  Public Comment: Shirley Tatsuno inquired about the possibility of allocating $20,000 from
  CDBG funds to support Family Promise of San Gabriel Valley, an organization that assists
  families experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Mrs. Tatsuno also mentioned Habitat for
  Humanity and expressed hope that the organization could collaborate with the City.

5. STAFF UPDATES

 Staff provided the HCDA with an update on the current funding status of the CDBG and
 HOME programs. Staff reached out to the local representative from the Los Angeles branch
 of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), who advised that the
 Consolidated Plans and Action Plans should proceed as usual. No changes in funding
 availability were reported at this time.

6. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE

  Lahiru Kodituwakku from the Community Health Alliance addressed the audience regarding
  smoke-free housing in multi-unit buildings in the City of Alhambra. According to Lahiru,
  Alhambra currently holds a C rating for secondhand smoke exposure, with one-third of the
  City's residents being affected by secondhand smoke.

7. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE

  None
  Page 2 of 3
 8. ADJOURNMENT: 8:14 p.m.

  Page 3 of 3
   OFFICIAL
  Minutes of the City of Alhambra’s
  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Regular Meeting of January 6, 2026
  CITY HALL • 111 S. FIRST ST.

Vice Chair McCammon called the meeting to order at: 6:30 p.m.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Committee Members Present:
  Lewis McCammon, Vice Chair  Manuel Armas
  Andrea Giese  Yvette Cardenas

  Committee Members Absent:
  Renee-Marie Alvarez

  City Staff Present:
  Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager
  Esteban Alvarez, Management Analyst

2. ELECTION OF HCDA COMMITTEE OFFICERS (CHAIR AND VICE CHAIR)

  Lewis McCammon was nominated for appointment as Chair of the HCDA Committee, and
  Manuel Armas was nominated for appointment as Vice Chair.

  Motion: A motion for approval was made by Committee Member Giese and seconded by
  Committee Member Cardenas.

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES: MARCH 4, 2025; SEPTEMBER 10, 2025

  City Staff Liaison Alvarez presented the March 4, 2025, and September 10, 2025, minutes to
  the Committee for review and approval. Staff noted that, due to a lack of quorum and prior
  meeting cancellations, the 2025 minutes were presented later than usual. It was requested
  that the March 4, 2025, minutes be brought back to the Committee for approval due to a
  correction needed in the roll call section, which mistakenly listed Bill Vallejos and Andrea
  Giese as both present and absent at that meeting.

  Motion: A motion for approval was made by Chair McCammon and seconded by Vice
  Chair Armas.

4. PROGRESS REPORTS

  City Staff Liaison Alvarez presented an oral report on the year-to-date progress of the Senior
  Case Management, Code Enforcement, Housing Rights Center, and Home Improvement
  programs. During the progress reports, Chair McCammon referenced he would bring up later
  in the meeting the Tenant Protection Act.

  Motion: Motion was made to receive and file the progress reports.

  Page 1 of 2
 5. AMENDMENT TO THE 2025-2026 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN TO ADD THE 2025
  STREET IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AS AN ELIGIBLE ACTIVITY

  Staff presented to the HCDA Committee a proposed Substantial Amendment to the 2025–
  2026 Annual Action Plan to establish a new infrastructure improvement activity in an
  amount not to exceed $374,114, funded by prior-year unspent CDBG funds. The proposal
  qualifies as a Substantial Amendment because it represents a cumulative change equal to or
  exceeding 25% of the City’s CDBG entitlement for the program year.

  The proposed 2025 Sidewalk Improvement Project is an eligible CDBG activity under the
  Public Facilities and Improvements category and would meet the National Objective of
  Limited Clientele Activities.

  The Substantial Amendment is scheduled to be presented to the City Council as a public
  hearing item on February 23, 2026.

  Motion: A motion for approval was made by Committee Member Giese and seconded by
  Committee Member Cardenas.

6. STAFF UPDATES

  Staff provided an update on the restructuring of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  membership, reducing it from ten to five members. An ordinance was presented to the City
  Council for first reading and approval on October 13, 2025, and for second reading and
  approval on October 27, 2025. The ordinance took effect 40 days after October 27, 2025.

  Staff also provided an update on the Section 108 Loan, noting that the loan remains pending
  HUD application review.

7. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE

  Gerardo Ivan Aguirre of Cardona Strategy introduced himself to the Committee. He shared
  that he is an alumnus of San Gabriel High School and expressed interest in becoming more
  involved with the City, including learning about its various committees and programs.

8. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE

  Chair McCammon provided the Committee with a copy of the Tenant Protection Act and
  expressed concern regarding evictions at 110 S. Chapel Avenue. He indicated an interest in
  exploring programs to support renters and stated that he would bring additional information
  to a future HCDA meeting for review and discussion.

9. ADJOURNMENT: The meeting was adjourned at 7:46 p.m. upon a motion by Chair
  McCammon, seconded by Committee Member Giese.

  Page 2 of 2
   OFFICIAL
  Minutes of the City of Alhambra’s
  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Regular Meeting of February 3, 2026
  CITY HALL • 111 S. FIRST ST.

Chair McCammon called the meeting to order at: 6:32 p.m.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Committee Members Present:
  Lewis McCammon, Chair  Manuel Armas , Vice Chair
  Andrea Giese  Yvette Cardenas

  Committee Members Absent:
  Renee-Marie Alvarez

  City Staff Present:
  Esteban Alvarez, Management Analyst

2. PROGRESS REPORTS
  City Staff Liaison Alvarez presented an oral report on the year-to-date progress of the Senior
  Case Management, Code Enforcement, Housing Rights Center, and Home Improvement
  programs. Following the presentation, Chair McCammon suggested correcting a minor
  typographical error in Item #7 of the Code Enforcement Division’s December 2025 report.
  Staff noted the correction and indicated it would be addressed in subsequent reports.

  Motion: Moved by Chair McCammon and seconded by Committee Member Giese to receive
  and file the reports.

3. 2026-2027 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN PROGRAM PREPARATION
  City Staff Liaison Alvarez presented a PowerPoint presentation that included an overview of
  the City’s Consolidated Plan goals, an overview of the CDBG and HOME programs,
  objectives and HUD-established funding caps for CDBG and HOME. The presentation also
  covered the City’s estimated 2026–2027 CDBG and HOME funding levels, including an
  alternative estimate incorporating a potential Section 108 loan, the City’s funding rationale,
  planning considerations, and a review of the City’s updated Low-/Moderate-Income map.
  The presentation was intended to educate the HCDA Committee on the City’s CDBG and
  HOME programs and to prepare the Committee for an upcoming meeting on the Fiscal Year
  2026–2027 Action Plan prior to submittal to City Council in May 2026.

  Comments were received from Committee Member Cardenas, who requested clarification
  regarding CDBG and HOME Administration, as well as the CHDO reserve set-aside,
  including its purpose.

  Chair McCammon expressed interest in exploring a rental or homebuyer assistance program
  for low-income households and referenced the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance and the
  Inclusionary Housing Fund.
  Page 1 of 2
 4. STAFF UPDATES
  Staff Liaison Alvarez reported that at the next regularly scheduled meeting, the Committee
  will be joined by the City’s CDBG consultant, Veronica Tam and Associates. Community
  stakeholders will be invited by the consultant to attend the meeting and provide input as the
  City begins the development of the 2026–2027 CDBG and HOME Action Plan.

  Mr. Alvarez also provided an update on the Section 108 Loan and noted that HUD is
  currently closed due to the government shutdown.

5. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  There were no members of the public in attendance, and no public comments were received.

6. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE
  Chair McCammon stated that he will return at the next meeting with additional information
  regarding the City’s Inclusionary Housing Fund and the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance for
  presentation to the Committee. No further comments were received from the Committee.

7. ADJOURNMENT: The meeting was adjourned at 7:30 p.m. upon motion by Chair
  McCammon, seconded by Committee Member Cardenas.

 CDBG:
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT

•  CDBG Primary Objective: Viable communities, principally for low/mod persons through decent housing,
  suitable living environment, and economic opportunity. REGS… 24 CFR Part 570
•  CDBG entitlement communities primarily use funds for housing and public improvement projects. New
  housing construction, income payments, equipment, maintenance PROHIBITED.
•  Activity outcomes must result in:
  •  Benefit low/mod persons (80% of Area Median Income)
  •  Low Mod Area: Residential and benefit all residents of area… water, sewer, parks, community centers... 51%
  LMI Census Tracts.
  •  Low Mod Clientele: Specific including seniors, disabled, homeless, AIDS, battered spouses… 51%
  “documented” as LMI or exclusive.
  •  Low Mod Housing: Rehab and homebuyer assistance… Documented based on unit occupancy.
  •  LMI Jobs: Job creation and retention (difficult).

  •  Prevent or eliminate slum and blight
  •  Meet urgent need
•  20% Max for Administration. 15% Max for Public Services.
•  Overall, 70% of CDBG expenditures must benefit low mod persons or HUD will require repayment.
•  Expenditure timeliness.
 HOME:
HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIP

•  HOME Primary Objective: Decent, Affordable Housing for Low Income People
•  HOME Program consists of four housing programs.
  •  Homeowner Rehab*
  •  Housing Construction
  •  Homebuyer
  •  Tenant Based Rental Assistance (Restricted)
•  100% of HOME funds must assist low-income households. All household income is counted.
•  The equivalent of at least 15% must go to CHDOs – Set aside must be owned, developed,
  sponsored units.
•  Commit funds within 2 years. Expend funds within 5 years.
•  10% Cap for HOME Administration.

*Current Alhambra HOME Programs
